title: Pricing of Climate Risk Insurance: Regulation and Cross-Subsidies
abstract: Homeowners’ insurance, a $15 trillion market by coverage, provides households financial protection from climate losses. Insurance premiums (rates) are subject to significant regulations at a state level in the United States. Using novel data on filings made by insurers to regulators, we propose a metric to quantify the extent of regulation in individual states. We provide evidence of decoupling of insurance rates from their underlying risks and identify regulation as a driving force behind this pattern. Rates are least reflective of risk in states we classify as "high friction", i.e. states where regulations appear most restrictive. We identify two sources behind the decoupling. First, in high friction states, rates have not adequately adjusted in response to the growth in losses. Second, insurers have cross-subsidized high friction states by raising rates in low friction states. Our results imply that households in low friction states are disproportionately bearing the risks of households in high friction states. More broadly, our findings question whether insurance rates can play a useful role in steering climate adaptation and whether households will have continued access to insurance.
abstract_zh: 房主保险按保额计算是一个规模达15万亿美元的市场，为家庭提供抵御气候损失的财务保障。在美国，保险费率（保费）受到各州层面的严格监管。利用保险公司向监管机构提交的新的文件数据，我们提出了一项用于量化各州监管程度的指标。我们提供了证据，表明保险费率与其潜在风险出现了脱钩，并认定监管是造成这一格局的驱动因素。在我们归类为“高摩擦”（即监管看似最为严格的州）的州，保险费率对风险的反映程度最低。我们识别出造成脱钩的两个来源。第一，在高摩擦州，保险费率并未充分地随损失增长而调整。第二，保险公司通过提高低摩擦州的费率，对高摩擦州进行了交叉补贴。我们的结果表明，低摩擦州的家庭不成比例地承担了高摩擦州家庭的风险。更广泛地说，我们的发现对保险费率能否在引导气候适应方面发挥有益作用，以及家庭能否持续获得保险，提出了质疑。

title: When Insurers Exit: Climate Losses, Fragile Insurers, and Mortgage Markets
abstract: Despite growing climate losses, Americans continue to move into high risk areas. This paper uses a range of natural experiments to show how mispricing of climate risk in mortgages and property insurance creates large taxpayer exposures and leads to excess credit flows to risky areas. Our central finding is that the government-sponsored enterprises' (GSEs) policies for evaluating property insurers are a crucial source of this mispricing. We assemble a comprehensive new dataset on both mortgages and insurance to analyze these dynamics in Florida from 2009-2018. We begin by documenting a breakdown in the quality of insurance provision, with new under-capitalized and under-diversified insurers dominating insurance markets. These fragile insurers have high rates of insolvency, which we show causally increases mortgage defaults after natural disasters. We find that the GSEs' reliance on third-party ratings of insurers leads them to accept insurance from companies at high risk of insolvency without pricing for it. This creates large taxpayer exposures, with an estimated 25% of the GSEs' expected losses in Florida coming from insurance fragility. Most starkly, we show that private lenders strategically respond to the GSE mispricing. Mortgage denial rates are sensitive to insurance quality in the jumbo segment where loans are retained, but not in the conforming segment where loans are offloaded to the GSEs. Our estimates imply that 1 in 4 GSE-eligible conforming mortgages would not have been originated by private lenders if they internalized insurance fragility risk at origination.
abstract_zh: 尽管气候损失日益增加，美国人仍持续迁入高风险地区。本文利用一系列自然实验表明，抵押贷款和财产保险中对气候风险的定价偏差会造成巨大的纳税人风险敞口，并导致信贷过度流向高风险地区。我们的核心发现是，政府支持企业（GSE）用于评估财产保险公司的政策，是这种定价偏差的关键来源。我们整理了一个涵盖抵押贷款和保险的全面新数据集，用于分析2009至2018年佛罗里达州的这些动态。我们首先记录了保险供给质量的下降：资本不足、业务分散不足的新保险公司主导了保险市场。这些脆弱的保险公司破产率很高，我们表明，这会在自然灾害之后因果性地增加抵押贷款违约。我们发现，政府支持企业依赖第三方对保险公司的评级，从而接受了破产风险高的公司提供的保险，却未对此进行定价。这造成了巨大的纳税人风险敞口，估计佛罗里达州政府支持企业的预期损失中有25%源自保险的脆弱性。最为突出的是，我们表明私人贷款机构会对政府支持企业的定价偏差做出战略性反应。在保留贷款的巨额贷款（jumbo）细分市场中，抵押贷款拒绝率对保险质量敏感；而在贷款被转售给政府支持企业的合格贷款（conforming）细分市场中，则不敏感。我们的估计表明，如果私人贷款机构在发放贷款时将保险脆弱性风险内部化，那么符合政府支持企业条件的合格抵押贷款中，将有四分之一不会由私人贷款机构发放。

title: Perspectives on Insurance and Climate Risk
abstract: Property insurance is central to managing rising risks from climate change, particularly for households whose homes are their biggest asset. Yet recent disruptions in insurance markets--such as, sharply rising premiums, rationing, and growing insurance fragility--have raised concerns about their long-term viability. These disruptions create new channels through which climate losses can propagate through housing and financial markets, affecting the distribution of climate risk and stability of the broader economy.   This review highlights emerging evidence and proposes research directions to advance the homeowners insurance agenda by integrating insurance into the broader climate finance, household finance, and macro-finance literature.
abstract_zh: 财产保险是管理气候变化带来的日益增长风险的核心，对于住房是其最大资产的家庭而言尤其如此。然而，近期保险市场的动荡，例如保费急剧上涨、保险配给以及保险脆弱性加剧，引发了人们对其长期可行性的担忧。这些动荡开辟了新的渠道，气候损失可通过这些渠道在住房和金融市场中传导，影响气候风险的分布以及整体经济的稳定性。本综述梳理了新出现的证据，并提出了研究方向，旨在通过将保险纳入更广泛的气候金融、家庭金融和宏观金融文献，推动房主保险的研究议程。

title: The Market for Sharing Interest Rate Risk: Quantities and Asset Prices
